assessment_summary: I validated the Audiominer installation against Installation.md (Docker Compose CPU method). Inspection confirmed the v2.4.0 repo at /workspace (commit e962370) with the documented template in deployments/example-opencode; .env contains the placeholder HF_TOKEN as stated. All four expected containers are running from the documented compose command, images were pulled from registry.opencode.de (anonymously, as the summary noted) plus library/redis:7. Both documented access points (8090 public UI, 8091 admin UI) serve the Audiominer frontend (HTTP 200). For operational evidence beyond file existence, I performed a live end-to-end test of the documented file workflow: copied a WAV into watch/, and observed the full pipeline — fs-watcher FileCreatedEvent → job creation → ASR RUNNING with language detection → job DONE with complete segment/word results → .txt and .srt transcripts written next to the source file with accurate content — completing in ~100 s. I also inspected service logs (Redis persistence normal, fs-watcher job-done events, ASR thread pool success:2 failed:0) and the modified asr-service.cpu.default.yml (presets block, consistent with the v2.5.1 image requirement stated in the summary). One significant event occurred: during my first live test the ASR service was OOM-killed (exit 137, dmesg confirmed ~6.9 GB RSS on a 7.6 GB host) while reloading the 4.23 GiB whisper large-v3 model after its idle cache eviction; I restarted the stack with the exact documented command (permitted normal startup) and confirmed fully normal operation, including completion of the previously interrupted job. This OOM episode is an environmental RAM limitation of the CPU large-v3 preset on the test host, not an installation defect. Known limitation: diarization is disabled due to the placeholder HF token (gated pyannote models return 401), as disclosed in the installation summary; a real token would enable it. All of my test artifacts were removed from watch/. Based on the running services, responsive UIs, and a live-verified transcription pipeline, the installation is complete and operational per the guide.
